reviews.reason: Libsecret and pkg-config installation is present before desktop build and non-server tests. Keep GitHub-hosted runners, fork ledger checks and fork branch triggers instead of upstream Blacksmith infrastructure. Server test shards remain separate. Fork-only authoring guards block against the selected head's upstream base; a pushed historical rewrite can suppress replayed authoring warnings only after proving its full tree equals the live fork source. Every other branch is offered the rebase-rehearsal scope, which suppresses them only after the scan proves the head omits the trunk and sits on a tagged upstream commit the trunk has not reached. The separately named live-upstream scan stays advisory so unrelated upstream drift does not fail a PR. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260905.1290: the fork adopts upstream's repo-wide knip:check step, and declines the setup-apt-mirrors action and the Blacksmith mirror rewrite because every fork job runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners where those mirror files do not exist.

Libsecret and pkg-config are installed before preflight tests and Linux artifact build; ImageMagick remains installed in the build job. Keep Linux x64 AppImage-only fork releases, fork stable/nightly versioning and pruning; upstream multi-platform signing and publication do not apply. The release checkout is now recorded before dependency setup, expected assets come from the actual build, and an always-run fork outcome job verifies tag/asset publication and retains failures for release-only retry. Runner-temporary export paths stay in step scope where the runner context is valid, with one shared filename for retention and upload; the required semantic guard keeps an unconditional nonempty receipt check between collection and upload, while missing upload inputs remain a hard error. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260905.1290 with no fork change: the setup-apt-mirrors steps target Blacksmith runners the fork does not use, and the Visual Studio Spectre component rename only affects the Windows build the Linux-only fork release never runs.
